---
title: "About"
---

I grew up wanting to know why things move the way they do. That curiosity
eventually became a PhD: I build algorithms that find the fastest way a
vehicle can move without asking for more grip than it has. I'm a PhD
candidate in the Doctoral Program in Materials, Mechatronics and Systems
Engineering ([DRMMSE](https://www.unitn.it/drmmse)) at the [University of
Trento](https://webapps.unitn.it/du/it/Persona/PER0221571/Didattica), where
my days split between optimal control theory, C++, and convincing a solver
to converge.

The common thread across everything I have worked on - minimum lap time
simulation, real-time velocity planning, maneuver negotiation for
self-driving cars - is the same question asked at different scales: given
the physics a vehicle actually has, what is the fastest, safest thing it can
do right now, and can the answer arrive fast enough to be useful. Off the
clock, I trade the desk for a mountain: climbing, skiing, mountain biking,
or grilling for whoever is around.

## What I work on

- Optimal control for minimum-time trajectory and velocity planning
- Motion planning and sampling-based algorithms for autonomous and racing vehicles
- Advanced Driver-Assistance Systems (ADAS) and safety assurance
- Vehicle dynamics and multibody modeling
- Multi-sensor, hardware-in-the-loop and real-vehicle testing

## Collaborations

- [DRIVEWISE](https://drivewise.github.io) - Prof. Francesco Biral's research group at the University of Trento; my primary research collaboration.
- [neu4mes](https://neu4mes.github.io) - collaboration on neural-model-structured frameworks for autonomous driving. Principal investigator: Prof. Gastone Pietro Rosati Papini at the University of Trento.
- [AVS](https://www.mos.ed.tum.de/en/avs/home/) - Autonomous Vehicle Systems Laboratory, TUM. Principal investigator: [Prof. Johannes Betz](https://www.mos.ed.tum.de/en/avs/team/prof-dr-ing-johannes-betz/); visiting researcher, 2025.
